note: What the phase A gate added (register decisions 409-414): --scene and the bare smoke test, the eye that runs leastAlignedAxis's third case, and the per-card expectation in the harness. Two survivors are declared, each with its reason; neither is a hole a test could close: one only hides another file's mutant, which that file's pass then reports, and one is equivalent, measured.

mutants.name: the bare scene draws the grid's lines after all
mutants.why: Drawing the lines in the bare scene changes nothing a test reads: the run is still valid, and the frame is not looked at. What it does is blind orbsim_smoke_bare to a resolve pass that never pushes its exposure, the defect the bare scene exists for (decision 409) -- and m1-15.json names orbsim_smoke_bare as that mutant's judge, so the blindness is reported by m1-15's next pass, which runs whenever main.cpp changes. Declared by decision 414, 2026-10-07.

mutants.name: leastAlignedAxis's third case returns x
mutants.why: Caught by the grid-400km golden, measured 2026-10-07 on the RTX A2000 (decision 416), which corrects decision 413: the probe's eye is 400 km above 6 degrees south, so z is its least-aligned axis and the case is taken. Any axis not parallel to the eye gives the same circle -- returning x passed every horizon case in test_planetary_grid, which checks that the points lie on it -- but not the same drawn line: the axis chooses where the 720 segments start, and x moves that start 83.87 degrees round the circle, 0.74 of a 0.5-degree segment off the original vertices, so a few pixels of the horizon move (largest 53/255, mean 0.00019/255). Not yet run on the RX 7900 XTX, whose own golden judges it at its next pass.
